Rugby.title: 'I can't wait to get started': Edinburgh appoint ex-Scotland international as new head coach
Rugby.summary: Scotland Under-21 coach Louise Dalgliesh has been appointed head coach of Edinburgh Rugby in the Celtic Challenge.
Rugby.body:
Scotland Under-21 coach Louise Dalgliesh has been appointed head coach of Edinburgh Rugby in the Celtic Challenge. A 67-cap Scotland international during her playing career, she joined the capital side from club partner the University of Edinburgh, where she served as Head of Performance for Women’s Rugby.

Dalgliesh replaces Claire Cruickshank at Edinburgh, who was recently appointed as Scottish Rugby’s first-ever Women’s National Academy Manager. The former Scotland international has worked for Japan Women as an assistant coach at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2021 [hosted in 2022] and as an assistant for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club Sale Sharks. In May 2025 Dalgliesh was appointed head coach of Scotland U20/U21.

Rugby.title: Ex-SA coach on the 3 things Springboks must fix before facing All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Nick Mallett has identified three areas South Africa can “definitely get better” in before facing the All Blacks, with the former Springboks...
Rugby.body:
Nick Mallett has identified three areas South Africa can “definitely get better” in before facing the All Blacks, with the former Springboks head coach calling for improvements in their lineout, attack and contestable kicking.

South Africa edged Argentina 17-10 in Buenos Aires on Saturday in their final match before their attention turns to New Zealand and the Greatest Rivalry. The victory at Estadio José Amalfitani was far from flawless, with Los Pumas making life uncomfortable for the world champions for large periods before the visitors eventually secured the win following a nervey final play.

Rugby.title: Rugby union's sniffiness around making money is exhausting
Rugby.summary: There has been a curious sniffiness around Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, as if South Africa and New Zealand have committed some breach of rugby etiquette by discovering...
Rugby.body:
A “branded, fundraising exercise”, according to The Times. The commercial imperatives have been “hammered home”, according to The Guardian. Elsewhere, the phrase “cash grab” has inevitably appeared.

There has been a curious sniffiness around Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, as if South Africa and New Zealand have committed some breach of rugby etiquette by discovering that people might pay good money to watch the two best teams in the world play each other.

Rugby.title: Black Ferns XV name 23-strong squad to battle Black Ferns in Wellington
Rugby.summary: Blair Baxter has included five capped Black Ferns in his Black Ferns XV squad ahead of this weekend's one-off clash.
Rugby.body:
Blair Baxter has included five capped Black Ferns in his Black Ferns XV squad ahead of this weekend’s one-off clash. On Friday afternoon, the Black Ferns XV will take on the Black Ferns at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt, Wellington. Nine players who represented the Black Ferns XV in 2025 have been selected in Whitney Hanson’s Black Ferns squad for upcoming O’Reilly Cup, Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry and WXV Global Series fixtures.

“This is a strong squad that has a balance of talent and potential with a shared ambition of representing the Black Ferns,” Baxter said. “This fixture is a great opportunity for these players to experience what will look and feel like a Test week. It’s also a chance for us to establish a solid foundation for Black Ferns XV as we build towards the first-ever British & Irish Lions Women’s Series next year.”

Rugby.title: Rennie reveals why Will Jordan and Tyrel Lomax are yet to feature in South Africa
Rugby.summary: When asked about the Sharks team selection methodology, Rennie pinpointed why three players won't feature in either of the first two RGR contests.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie is not taking any risks with two of his more experienced players ahead of the first Test against the Springboks next week. Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour is now well underway after the All Blacks squeezed past the Stormers in Cape Town, before taking on the Sharks in the side’s second tour match.

The All Blacks, who were far from perfect against the Cape Town-based United Rugby Championship side, have made several changes ahead of the Sharks clash, with only seven players from Saturday’s opener backing up.

Rugby.title: Queensland pair have Suaalii under pressure to retain midfield role
Rugby.summary: Hunter Paisami is hungry for a hometown farewell as calls mount for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to switch to the wing under new Wallabies coach Les Kiss.
Rugby.body:
Hunter Paisami is hungry for a hometown farewell as calls mount for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to switch to the wing under new Wallabies coach Les Kiss. With Len Ikitau (ankle) injured, the pair formed the midfield partnership in Australia’s hard-fought 35-32 defeat of Japan in Osaka on Saturday.

Paisami, who was coached by Kiss at the Queensland Reds for the last three seasons, made the most of his call-up as one of the side’s best starters alongside impressive lock Josh Canham.

Rugby.title: Wallabies won't shy away from 'license to play' under Kiss
Rugby.summary: Australia defied a 20-minute red card and brutal heat and humidity to pip Eddie Jones's plucky Japan 35-32 and ensure the Kiss era began with victory on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies won’t be spooked off the Les Kiss way after avoiding an Osaka disaster, pledging to commit after being “given a licence to play” by the new coach. Australia defied a 20-minute red card and brutal heat and humidity to pip Eddie Jones’s plucky Japan 35-32 and ensure the Kiss era began with victory on Saturday.

Flyhalf Declan Meredith battled all night to make ground with his exit kicks, and the fluency shown in a last-start flogging of Italy wasn’t there. But, after winning just five of 15 Tests under Joe Schmidt last year, they did enough and will meet Japan again in friendlier conditions in Townsville this Saturday afternoon, hoping to find a higher gear.

Rugby.title: World Cup winner recalled into Springboks squad following injuries
Rugby.summary: Stormers flanker and Springbok Deon Fourie has been called into the Springboks ahead of the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Stormers flanker and Springbok Deon Fourie has been called into the Springboks ahead of the Greatest Rivalry series according to a report by SA Rugby Mag. The 39-year-old was industrious for the Stormers against the All Blacks on Friday night playing openside flanker and will now potentially take on the Test team.

He provides loose forward and hooker cover for the Springboks who are awaiting scans on captain Siya Kolisi who was forced off the field early in Buenos Aires against Argentina.

Rugby.title: 'Worried': Justin Marshall flags concern for Dave Rennie after Stormers clash
Rugby.summary: "Guys like Peter Lakai really fronted up. Fabian Holland, how good was he, having not played a lot of rugby, and equally you can just see the balance of that side and players that hadn't played a lot.
Rugby.body:
Former All Black halfback Justin Marshall believes there are multiple areas of concern for Dave Rennie after their 17-point triumph over the Stormers in Cape Town. Rennie and the All Blacks overcame a physical challenge by the United Rugby Championship side on Saturday morning NZT, where they were put under enormous amounts of pressure on several fronts.

The All Blacks were penalised and yellow-carded on multiple occasions by English referee Karl Dickson, which highlighted areas where Rennie’s side must improve before the four-Test series against the Springboks.

Rugby.title: Report: Scott Robertson offered shock NRL head coaching role
Rugby.summary: “The ball’s in Razor’s court at the moment, but I don’t want to push him or pressure him in any way."
Rugby.body:
The New Zealand Herald has reported that former All Blacks head coach Scott Robertson has been offered an NRL head coaching role with the Southern Orcas. The proposed Christchurch-based NRL franchise, according to club president Sir Graham Lowe, has tabled a four-year deal to Robertson to become the head coach.

The 51-year-old has been without a role since departing the All Blacks frame in January 2026, apart from a short stint with the Barbarians alongside Felipe Contepomi. “We’re well aware that he’s not coached rugby league before, but he’s certainly got a good handle on rugby league and has been looking at it closely and studying it closely for a long time; that’s quite obvious,” Lowe told the Herald.

Rugby.title: Whitney Hansen unveils new-look Black Ferns squad for remainder of 2026
Rugby.summary: "We’re also thrilled to welcome our new Black Ferns, who will bring different strengths to our environment on and off the field,” Hansen said.
Rugby.body:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has revealed her 31-strong squad for the rest of 2026, making nine changes from the Pacific Four Series. Hansen’s side will take on the Black Ferns XV this Friday at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt, before beginning to prepare for the O’Reilly Cup presented by Bupa against Australia.

The Black Ferns will then face South Africa as part of the RGR tour, before the WXV Global Series gets underway in September against France. The nine changes feature several standout performers from Super Rugby Aupiki, including Chiefs outside back Shyrah Tuliau-Tua’a, Blues lock Amarante Sititi, loosehead prop Ngano Tavake, loose forward Elinor-Plum King, and Matatu outside-back Maia Davis.

Rugby.title: The three performers of the week from Hilux NPC round two
Rugby.summary: Hannah started 13 of his 15 appearances for the Crusaders in Super Rugby Pacific 2026, ranking among the top ten players in tackles (179) and lineouts (64).
Rugby.body:
Hawke’s Bay are the hottest commodity in the NPC after two rounds, posting a 50-19 win over Tasman at McLean Park in Napier, their second 50-point victory. The Magpies led 33-5 at halftime and were collectively outstanding, with lock Hunter Morrison continuing his eye-catching form and first-five Harry Godfery finding his feet after a long spell injured.

North Harbour aren’t going to be easybeats after thrashing Counties Manukau 59-19 on Thursday for just their fifth win since the start of 2024. Elsewhere, all other matches were decided by less than a converted try.

Rugby.title: 'It was a matter of life and death' Former Springbok reveals career-altering tragedy
Rugby.summary: Former Springbok wing Sbu Nkosi has revealed that the death of his two children at birth sat behind the mental health crisis that engulfed his time at the Vodacom Bulls and left him fearing for his own safety.
Rugby.body:
Former Springbok wing Sbu Nkosi has revealed that the death of his two children at birth sat behind the mental health crisis that engulfed his time at the Vodacom Bulls and left him fearing for his own safety.

Nkosi, a member of South Africa’s 2019 Rugby World Cup-winning squad, disappeared from public view in late 2022. The Bulls said he had been absent without leave for three weeks and that their last contact with him had come on November 11, prompting a missing-person case to be opened with the South African Police Service (SAPS).

Rugby.summary: Moana Pasifika enforcer Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa and Blues hooker Bradley Slater are set to make their All Blacks debuts off the bench.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has named his 23-man squad to take on the Sharks in Durban, with a bunch of changes from their first Greatest Rivalry Tour game against the Stormers.

Rennie has given Chiefs captain Luke Jacobson the opportunity to captain his country for the first time, after being named in the No.7 jersey for the second midweek clash. Moana Pasifika enforcer Semisi Tupou Ta’eiloa and Blues hooker Bradley Slater are set to make their All Blacks debuts off the bench. Emoni Narawa and Timoci Tavatavanawai also feature for the first time in 2026.

Rugby.title: Japan vs Wallabies: Dearns and Canham World XV locks, Gordon should start
Rugby.summary: The Wallabies are off to a winning start under new coach Les Kiss, overcoming a Miles Amatosero 20-minute red card in a tense 35-32 win over Japan.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies are off to a winning start under new coach Les Kiss, overcoming a Miles Amatosero 20-minute red card in a tense 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka. It’s the first time in 12 months that the Wallabies have successfully gone back-to-back with wins, following a 47-point triumph over Italy last month. They will chase more drought-breaking history next weekend, having not won three Tests in a row since the July internationals in 2024.

Next up for the Wallabies is another clash with the Brave Blossoms, with Townsville’s Queensland Country Bank Stadium hosting the fixture, 14 months out from Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 on home soil.

Rugby.summary: Tim Horan has called on Les Kiss to make two key changes after a nail-biting 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka, including a switch for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii.
Rugby.body:
Tim Horan has called on Les Kiss to make two key changes after a nail-biting 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka, including a switch for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, who the Wallabies great believes is being “wasted” at outside centre.

The Wallabies have started their new era under coach Kiss on a winning note, overcoming a red card to lock Miles Amatosero in a closely-fought Test. Japan captain Warner Dearns made it a one-score game in the dying stages, but the visitors did enough to secure the win.

Rugby.title: Four major surgeries in four years: Newest Wallaby's hard-earned Osaka debut
Rugby.summary: Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark.
Rugby.body:
Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark after a hard-earned debut in Osaka. Named on the bench, the Queensland Reds centre was made to wait more than 70 minutes before being thrust into the action and then defending furiously in a 35-32 Saturday night defeat of Japan.

The 27-year-old became Wallaby No.999 in the process, the honour coming despite Henry enduring four major surgeries in as many years. “It’s a great number, might have to talk to my wife about getting it tattooed,” said Henry, who has his surname inked on his forearm.

Tennis.title: Why I think Jack Draper should now skip the US Open after his first round loss at the Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: Why I think Jack Draper should now skip the US Open after his first round loss at the Cincinnati Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper lost again last night, meaning that of the last five tournaments he has entered, spanning five months, he has suffered four first-round exits. This is not nearly at the level we expect from the former world number four, but such a downturn is through no fault of his own.

Instead, this has been the cruel result of an injury he simply cannot fix, no matter what he tries. Rest has not resolved the bone bruising in his arm, and surgery would only make things worse. It’s the worst place for a professional athlete to be in, and it comes at a crucial time in Jack Draper’s career, just when he seemed set to be a mainstay at the apex for years to come.

It proved another difficult day for the former US Open semifinalist on his comeback from a longstanding bone bruising issue after he had broken down in tears during a defeat to Terence Atmane at last week's National Bank Open in Montreal.

Draper, in only his second match since he missed Wimbledon to continue a torrid injury-hit 12 months, had been two breaks up in the second set of his match with world number 64 Landaluce before he collapsed to exit the Masters 1000 event in the first round.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper ‘in difficult place’ after defeat by Martín Landaluce at Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper ‘in difficult place’ after defeat by Martín Landaluce at Cincinnati Open The Guardian
Tennis.body:
The minuscule amount of confidence and self-belief Jack Draper currently has to call upon in the most difficult period of his career was underscored in the first game of his opening match in Cincinnati. Draper began his service game by shanking a forehand into the back fence, which he followed up with two double faults. He immediately fell down a break and never recovered.

A few fleeting positive moments followed, but this miserable start set the tone for another excruciating day for the former world No 4 as he could not escape the mental fatigue borne out of battling serious injury for 15 months and counting. Draper fell 6-3, 7-5 to Martín Landaluce, the world No 64.

Tennis.title: Draper slumps to first-round loss in Cincinnati
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper slumps to a straight sets defeat in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after leading 5-2 in the second set.
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper slumped to a straight sets defeat in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after leading 5-2 in the second set. Playing in his first match since breaking down in tears during his return from injury last week, the Briton looked set to force a deciding set against Spain's Martin Landaluce.

But the former world number four spurned six set points as 20-year-old Landaluce won five straight games to clinch a 6-3 7-5 victory. Draper, 24, finished with 47 unforced errors and 12 double faults against the world number 64.

Tennis.title: Cincinnati Open: Jan Choinski and Jack Draper lose as Cameron Norrie progresses

Jan Choinski and Jack Draper were knocked out of the first round of the Cincinnati Open on Thursday as fellow Briton Cameron Norrie progressed. Choinski bowed out after a hard-fought contest with Argentina's Thiago Agustin Tirante, with all three sets going to a tie-break.

The match lasted nearly three hours before Tirante won 7-6 (11-9) 6-7 (7-9) 7-6 (7-4) against Choinski, the world number 77. Draper led 5-2 in the second set against Martin Landaluce but the Spaniard won the next five games to clinch a 6-3 7-5 victory.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper Has the World in His Sights: "My Tennis Hasn’t Gone Anywhere”
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper Has the World in His Sights: "My Tennis Hasn’t Gone Anywhere” Esquire
Tennis.body:
This month, Jack Draper hopes to compete at the US Open. The journey to this point has been eventful: in the spring, he announced that Andy Murray would be joining his coaching team, though the 24-year-old  later had to withdraw from Wimbledon because of a recurrent arm injury. In this profile, from our July/August issue, the latest cover star of Esquire Edge discusses his tumultuous past year, teaming up with Murray and his enviable fashion credentials.

Jack Draper is, as far as I’m aware, the only man to have ever performed a body-popping routine on a Wimbledon show court. The occasion was the 2018 boys singles final, and it was the first time I saw Draper — then a slim, rangy 16-year-old — strike a tennis ball. Naturally right-handed, he played as a leftie and seemed to crush forehands off both sides. But it was his swagger that stayed with me, and probably many of the 10,000 spectators on Wimbledon’s Court One. He didn’t win the title, against Taiwanese top seed Tseng Chun-hsin, but the body-popping — busted out after Draper theatrically saved a match point — suggested he was very much at home at the world’s most famous tennis tournament.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper: I cried because I had hit rock bottom
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper: I cried because I had hit rock bottom Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper said his on-court breakdown as he attempted yet another comeback to the tennis tour was because he had "hit rock bottom". Draper will be in action on Thursday in the opening round of the Cincinnati Masters as he attempts to continue his return from a long-term injury to his racket arm. Last week, in his first match since Eastbourne, Draper wept for an entire changeover in his three-set defeat by Terence Atmane at the Canadian Open.

It was his first appearance for almost six weeks as a result of the ongoing problems with his left arm, which have affected him since spring last year, and he has admitted that he "did not recognise the player out on court", thus prompting the sudden outpouring of emotion.

Tennis.title: 'I have to start again' - Draper ready for comeback after hitting 'rock bottom'
Tennis.summary: 'I have to start again' - Draper ready for comeback after hitting 'rock bottom' TNT Sports
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper says he feels like he has hit ”rock bottom” this summer but is ready to "start again" as he explained his tearful reaction during his recent first-round Canadian Open defeat. The former British No. 1 has struggled with a persistent arm injury over the last year, sidelining him for long periods.

Draper's ranking dropped as low as No. 160, having reached world No. 4 in 2025, the year he won a maiden ATP Masters 1000 title at Indian Wells. The 24-year-old returned to the court in Montreal this month for his first appearance since June, but he appeared to suffer from recurring discomfort and ultimately lost 6-3 2-6 6-2 against Terence Atmane.

Tennis.summary: Iga Swiatek will meet Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final after both players battled through their semi-finals in three sets.
Tennis.body:
Iga Swiatek will meet Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final after both players battled through their semi-finals in three sets. Six-time Grand Slam champion Swiatek withstood an Elina Svitolina comeback attempt to seal a 6-3 1-6 6-3 win in Toronto and reach her first WTA final of the season.

The Pole, 25, had not reached a WTA 1,000 final since winning Cincinnati 12 months ago and had only reached one semi-final this year. "It hasn't been an easy season, probably the toughest one in my life," said seventh seed Swiatek.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper: ‘When you reach rock bottom like that you can come back up again’
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper: ‘When you reach rock bottom like that you can come back up again’ The Guardian
Tennis.body:
Those painful images have relentlessly spread to all corners of the internet. Deep in the final set of the first-round match at the Canadian Open against Térence Atmane just over a week ago, 15 months of pent up emotion erupted. Two games from defeat, Draper spent the entire changeover in tears.

This was a devastating and alarming sight. Injuries had already defined so much of Draper’s career, but the uncertainty of trying to recover from a bone bruise injury to his left arm over the past year has been more challenging than anything he has experienced. All of his efforts since last July have been focused on trying to find a way to compete consistently at the highest level again, to no avail.

Alcaraz remains at world No 2 despite not having played competitively since April, when he withdrew in Barcelona because of the injury. The problem prevented Alcaraz from defending his French Open title and denied him the chance to attempt to win Wimbledon for a third time.

Tennis.title: Rybakina comeback knocks Osaka out of Canadian Open
Tennis.summary: Elena Rybakina comes back from a set and a break down to beat Naomi Osaka in three sets in their Canadian Open quarter-final.
Tennis.body:
Elena Rybakina came back from a set and a break down to beat Naomi Osaka in three sets in their Canadian Open quarter-final. Four-time Grand Slam winner Osaka had won the first set and was 4-2 up in the second before her Kazakh rival came back to win 4-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 in two hours and 33 minutes.

"I was just trying to fight," said Rybakina, whose 72 unforced errors were her most in a match this season. "The first game was really tough because it cost me the set, and then in the second I was just trying to stay closer to the score, even if I'm losing. I'm super happy that I won this match."

Tennis is one of the most traditional sports there is, but of late changes have been made to try and bring it into the modern world. These have been in an effort to provide a greater fan experience, increase revenue and exposure, and, most importantly, give their star players what they want.

Tennis.title: World number one Sinner to miss Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: World number one Jannik Sinner withdraws from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month.
Tennis.body:
World number one Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month. The 24-year-old Italian won his fifth Grand Slam singles title by beating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final last month, but has not played since.

"After consulting with my doctors and my team, I have to announce that I need to withdraw from the Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati," Sinner said. "My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept I'm not ready to compete yet.

Tennis.title: National Bank Open: In-form Cam Norrie defeated by Arthur Fils in Montreal while Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock Canadian Open loss
Tennis.summary: National Bank Open: In-form Cam Norrie defeated by Arthur Fils in Montreal while Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock Canadian Open loss Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Britain's Cameron Norrie has been knocked out of the National Bank Open at the last-16 stage following a 6-2 7-6 (10-8) defeat by Arthur Fils in Montreal. The French 18th seed looked dominant early on in the Montreal contest, utilising his powerful serve well to wrap up the first set without much hassle.

Norrie stepped up a gear in the second, matching Fils' power to force a tie-break. Despite creating two set-point opportunities, Norrie was ultimately unable to convert when it mattered and Fils sealed the win in one hour and 43 minutes.

Tennis.body:
Women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffered a surprise defeat in the Canadian Open weeks before she begins her US Open title defence, while Britain's Cameron Norrie also bowed out in the last 16.

Sabalenka lost 7-6 (7-3) 4-6 6-4 to Russia's Ekaterina Alexandrova in a match lasting almost two and a half hours in Toronto. The Belarusian recovered from a set down to force a decider, but a double fault when serving to stay in the match handed the number 16 seed victory.

Scottie Scheffler equalled the course record with a nine-under-par 61 as he opened up a three-stroke lead at the end of the second round of the St Jude Championship in Memphis.

Golf.title: Inside the Lab: What I learned visiting Mitsubishi’s state-of-the-art KOBO facility
Golf.summary: Johnny Wunder visited Mitsubishi’s state-of-the-art testing facility in Carlsbad to explore a new way of looking at shaft fitting The post Inside the Lab: What I learned visiting Mitsubishi’s state-of-the-art KOBO facility appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Before we got into our testing, we stopped by Mitsubishi’s new KOBO facility in Carlsbad, California. The place is essentially an R&D playground filled with cameras, robots, and custom shaft-testing machines. It gives you a quick look at why what happens in the lab translates directly to finding the center of the face on the golf course.

For decades, the equipment side of the game has leaned on a very tidy, convenient narrative: if you swing fast, you need a heavier, stiffer shaft profile that launches low and kills spin. if you swing slower or struggle to get the ball airborne, you need a lighter, softer shaft that launches high. That makes some sense, but it doesn’t tell the full story.

Golf.title: This 63-year-old went viral at U.S. Amateur. Then went back to work
Golf.summary: Mike McCoy, 63, missed the stroke-play cut at the U.S. Amateur this week but still made a lot of new fans along the way. The post This 63-year-old went viral at U.S. Amateur. Then went back to work appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Sixty-three-old Mike McCoy was never going to win this 126th U.S. Amateur, not when he was giving up 50 yards off the tee to many players in the field, as he did in his two stroke-play rounds alongside 21-year-old U.S. Amateur champion Noah Maclauchlan and 39-year-old U.S. Mid-Amateur champion Brandon Holtz.

The first of those rounds, on Monday, came at Philadelphia Country Club, in Gladwyne, home to a beefy William Flynn design. McCoy made five bogeys and a double and signed for a five-over 75. On Tuesday, he and his partners headed about 6 miles due south for their second round, at storied Merion Golf Club, the star of this week’s show. McCoy had fewer blemishes on his card — three bogeys and a double — en route to a four-over 74. Nine over for 36 holes for the U.S. Senior Amateur champion was a commendable showing but still seven shots more than McCoy needed to join a playoff for a spot in the 64-player match-play field. By Wednesday afternoon, McCoy, who runs an insurance business, was back at his desk in West Des Moines, Iowa.

Golf.title: Do you slice the golf ball? This subtle backswing mistake could be why
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joe Plecker explains the subtle backswing flaw that may be causing you slice — and shows how to fix it. The post Do you slice the golf ball? This subtle backswing mistake could be why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When players come to me fighting a slice, the instinct is almost always to blame the swing. But more often than not, the swing itself is fine — it’s the clubface that’s off. Here’s the pattern I see as a player takes the club back: the face rotates “toe up” relative to their posture. It may look like the club is square (and feels square), but relative to their spine angle at the address, it’s actually open. That small discrepancy is enough to send the ball curving right for a right-handed player.

So, how do we fix this? You can start by trying this simple checkpoint drill. Take an alignment rod and stick it in the ground just behind the ball at address, angled to match your posture. This gives you a visual reference for where the clubface should be pointing as you swing back.

Golf.title: At U.S. Amateur, Merion’s secrets are hiding in a wondrous, windowless room
Golf.summary: Merion’s archives room, in a deep and hidden part of its twist-and-turns clubhouse, is managed by its resident historian, John Capers III. The post At U.S. Amateur, Merion’s secrets are hiding in a wondrous, windowless room appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — If you read Ann Patchett, you will seldom, if ever, encounter the four-letter word that draws you to this website. The author of “Bel Canto” and “Tom Lake” and a current New York Times bestseller, “Whistler,” has plenty of themes in her typing life without ever falling under the spell of ye olde game.

But Patchett’s brother-in-law is a golf pro. And Andy Brennan, the general manager of the bookstore Patchett owns in Nashville, is a golf bum with impeccable credentials. He has actually read John Daly’s “My Life In and Out of the Rough,” just as he has read the Bernard Darwin, Henry Longhurst and Herbert Warren Wind canon. Before he fell into the book business, Brennan was a course superintendent and a course builder. (He once made an ace on one of his own holes.) He has known about a strain of grass called Merion Blue forever, or at least 1971, or circa* 1971. It was in 1971 that Lee Trevino won his U.S. Open at Merion, in a playoff over Jack Nicklaus. Brennan also attended the 1981 U.S. Open at Merion. Classic busman’s holiday**. On Thursday he was back at Merion, for the Am. The U.S. Amateur.

Golf.title: YouTube Golf took over. Tour pros want their piece of the pie, too
Golf.summary: It was only a matter of time before pro golfers joined the YouTube ranks. Here's why they've decided to chase views, too. The post YouTube Golf took over. Tour pros want their piece of the pie, too appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
This article first appeared in the July/August issue of GOLF Magazine. In mid-March, the world’s leading golfing content creator — or is it content-creating golfer? — gazed through the windows of the media center at Steyn City, host of that week’s LIV Golf South Africa event in Johannesburg, where a horde of fans were leaning over each other, waiting for his autograph. Bryson DeChambeau had just shot 63, but his eyes said something more. As he waited for his turn at the press conference podium, we chatted for a few minutes — just long enough for him to dream aloud about reuniting professional golf.

The plan he’d devised — constructed, in part, via ChatGPT and Google Gemini — featured tournaments with a field of 104 players: 13 four-man PGA Tour teams competing alongside 13 four-man LIV Golf teams. Half the individual field would be cut after 36 holes — to appease Tiger Woods, DeChambeau said. The new league would be jointly owned by the PGA Tour, LIV and the players. And though it all seems like folly now that LIV may cease to exist in 2027, DeChambeau believed in it so resolutely because of the person he’d convinced of its legitimacy: YouTube CEO Neil Mohan.

Golf.title: This simple training aid helps perfect your weight shift
Golf.summary: If weight shift and transition are on your list of swing-improvement goals, Why Golf's Pressure Plate with Power Wedge gives instant feedback. The post This simple training aid helps perfect your weight shift appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the most difficult parts of changing your swing is trying to do it alone. That’s why having a second person like an instructor present can be invaluable, because the second set of eyes can help keep you — and your swing goals — in check.

But when you’re by yourself, sometimes it can be hard to tell if you’re managing to do what you think you’re doing. For those solo situations, using a training aid that offers feedback you can feel is so valuable. It empowers you to work on your swing when you’re alone, and still have the assurance that what you’re working on is correct.

Golf.body:
Several LIV Golf players have entered DP World Tour Q School as uncertainty over the league’s future continues. The rampant uncertainty that has enveloped LIV Golf for months has left many of the league’s biggest names and brightest talents pondering their futures, but some players may be ejected regardless.

With LIV’s team finale in Michigan now cancelled in all but an official statement, the league will convene for the final time in 2026 at the Chatham Hills Club in Indianapolis next week. And lost in the existential talk of LIV’s survival hopes in a post-Saudi era is what, in any typical week, would be a hugely consequential week on the fairways. At the start of the season, LIV increased its relegation positions from six to 11 to prove to the Official World Golf ranking board that the league was not a closed shop.

Golf.title: Rising golf star, 18, dies after brain haemorrhage

Golf.body:
Jessica Bang, a promising Australian golfer, has died at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage. Bang, who won her first professional event in just her fifth start earlier this year, was preparing for a tournament in Thailand on 1 August when she collapsed.

She was rushed to a hospital in Bangkok and had emergency brain surgery. After being in intensive care for nearly two weeks, she died on Thursday. The WPGA Tour of Australasia said Bang, who turned professional at the end of 2025, was an "outstanding young talent".

Golf.title: This U.S. Amateur is a glimpse into golf's future in more ways than you think
Golf.summary: Merion's U.S. Amateur hosting job has been commendable. If the right people are watching, it might also be repeatable. The post This U.S. Amateur is a glimpse into golf’s future in more ways than you think appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Let the record reflect, now and forever, that at least some things were not perfect about this U.S. Amateur. For one thing, the line at the merchandise tent was long and inventory for a handful of boutique golf brands ran low (’twas not the week to go looking for a cotton polo with a wicker basket logo). For another, the practice range was far from the golf course and not easy for the average fan to reach. And for a third, a small number of Merion members appeared miffed by the grave indignity of hosting one of the biggest events in golf at their home course … and surprised that such a pursuit involved welcoming real people to the golf course.

We speak these criticisms because complaints have been impressively hard to find at this 126th U.S. Amateur at the esteemed Merion Golf Club in Philadelphia. The tournament has been delightful, a mix of great talent and great drama and great pressure and great commitment to golf’s most elemental professional signifier: Amateur. The golf has been sublime, evidenced by heavy tournament favorite Miles Russell’s stunning round-of-64 departure on Wednesday afternoon. The golf course has been spectacular, a blend of hunter and kelly greens so perfectly coiffed and immaculately presented they’d make even Saquon Barkley blush. Hell, even the attire has been good — even if most of that belongs to the fedora-wearing, collar-popping early hero of tournament week, Matt Lowe. (Who revealed Wednesday afternoon that his U.S. Amateur virality was hiding far more substance than style.)

Golf.title: She made an albatross at her state amateur. Then she conceded one
Golf.summary: Lillian Guleserian made the unlikeliest of scores at the Massachusetts Women’s State Amateur. In a wild twist, so did her opponent. The post She made an albatross at her state amateur. Then she conceded one appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Scan Shannon Johnson’s scorecard from her quarterfinal match at the Massachusetts Women’s State Amateur on Thursday and one number will leap out at you: her 2 on the par-5 18th hole.

The rarest score in golf. A one-in-6 million shot, according to several published estimates. But this story isn’t really about Johnson — it’s about her opponent, 19-year-old Lillian Guleserian, who is a rising sophomore at Penn State, where she plays on the women’s golf team. Guleserian, who is from Westwood, Mass., has had herself a nice summer. In early June, she finished 5th at the Women’s Southern GA Amateur, which she quickly followed up with a win at the New England Women’s Amateur Championship. Then, late last month, came a 3rd-place finish at the Francis Ouimet Memorial Tournament.

Golf.body:
On Wednesday at the 2026 U.S. Amateur, Ryder Cowan earned perhaps the biggest upset of the week, beating star amateur Miles Russell 2 and 1 to advance to the round of 32 at historic Merion Golf Club.

Incredibly, Cowan pulled off the feat with a major handicap in the gear department: he had only two golf balls in his bag to start the day, only one of which was a new one. It turns out the U.S. Amateur contender “literally forgot golf balls” in his hotel room before heading to the course. Cowan explained the bizarre incident in his post-match press conference on Wednesday at Merion.

Golf.title: How Fat Perez and online creators are cashing in on golf's digital boom
Golf.summary: An online explosion has brought golf, in one form or another, to millions of new fans — and minted a new breed of celebrity in the process. The post How Fat Perez and online creators are cashing in on golf’s digital boom appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Before he lost 100 pounds and gained a million followers, Nick Stubbe was a beefy ex-collegiate golfer with an office job and an Instagram account on which he rarely posted. Weekdays, he worked as an accountant. Weekends, he knocked it around with friends on a rota of courses in Richmond, Va.

The routine suited the easygoing Stubbe, who liked his colleagues and loved his golf, playing to scratch with a buttery swing and a beer-league body that made him look as if he’d stumbled to the first tee from a tailgate. What he didn’t look like was a budding social media star, which was fine by him because he wasn’t trying to become one. The sponsorship deals, celebrity pro-ams, viral videos with Bryson DeChambeau — none of that was part of any plan because, well, there was no plan.

Golf.body:
An amateur golfer says he has "completely made a fool" of himself after admitting he faked making a hole-in-one at a tournament in the United States. Zach Holland was due to play in a two-person team competition at WingHaven Country Club in Missouri when he fraudulently placed the ball in the cup at the fourth hole earlier in the morning, before his round.

Holland, who is a plus-two handicap, had completed the first three holes when he told his group he was going to have to take a phone call as his grandmother was ill, so he would run ahead to the next tee and hit his shot first to keep up with the pace of play.

Golf.title: Is LIV Golf about to lose world ranking points?
Golf.summary: Is LIV Golf about to lose world ranking points? Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
LIV Golf waited nearly four years to secure Official World Golf Ranking points. But is that arrangement now in jeopardy? When LIV Golf finally ended its near-four year wait for world ranking points in February, those presiding over the “exhaustive” process provided a detailed explanation for their conclusions.

The Official World Golf Ranking body had eventually opted to limit points to only the top-10 finishers at each LIV event, an arrangement the breakaway league regarded as “unprecedented” victimization. But in a long-winded statement laying out its reasons, the OWGR board said it recognized a “number of areas where LIV Golf does not meet the eligibility standards set out”.

Golf.title: This curious Miles Russell decision in U.S. Amateur loss was tactical
Golf.summary: Miles Russell's 13th-hole birdie try in the U.S. Amateur's first round hit his opponent's mark. Here's why Russell didn't want it moved. The post This curious Miles Russell decision in U.S. Amateur loss was tactical appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Match play is all about swing moments: a smashed drive on a short par-4 that bounds up onto the green. A stuffed approach. A putt that lips in, or out. Ryder Cowan, the world’s 8th-ranked amateur and with a name made for head-to-head golf, experienced one of these moments — a decisive one — in his heavyweight, first-round bout with 4th-ranked Miles Russell at this 126th U.S. Amateur. As Cowan sized up his short-sided chip in juicy rough on the left side of the par-3 17th green, he had a 1-up lead on Russell — but also a horrid lie. Cowan chopped at it, advancing his ball all of about two inches.

Advantage, Russell, who after his own chip, from the back of the green, had about 10 feet left for his par. Cowan stared down at his ball and tried again. Out the ball popped, onto the green and . . . into the hole. Yep, another moment. Suddenly, Russell needed to hole his par try merely to extend the match. He didn’t. Cowan def. Russell, 2 and 1.

Golf.title: DP World Tour reportedly ready to fine and suspend LIV Golf members again in 2027, likely forcing decision ahead of Ryder Cup
Golf.summary: DP World Tour reportedly ready to fine and suspend LIV Golf members again in 2027, likely forcing decision ahead of Ryder Cup Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour is again taking a stand against LIV Golf. The European circuit has started notifying LIV Golf members that it will resume imposing heavy fines and suspensions as part of its conflicting events rule in 2027, according to The Athletic's Gabby Herzig. That will, in theory, force a select group of golfers to choose between the two leagues at a time in which the future of LIV Golf is incredibly uncertain.

There were eight LIV Golf members who were granted conditional releases to participate in DP World Tour events without fines or suspensions in February. Previously, at the height of the LIV Golf feud throughout the sport, golfers were hit with massive fines or suspensions for playing in unauthorized tournaments on the Saudi Arabian-backed venture. But the players — Tyrrell Hatton, Laurie Canter, Thomas Detry, Tom McKibbin, Adrian Meronk, Victor Perez, David Puig and Elvis Smylie — reached a deal to pay all previously incurred fines and play in extra DP World Tour events. That allowed them to compete on both the DP World Tour and LIV Golf in 2026.

ARDMORE, Pa. — It was not yet 11 on a still, warm Wednesday morning at Merion Golf Club, but Mike and Sherry Sands needed a drink. Could you blame them? On Tuesday evening, their son, Parker, a 20-year-old rising junior at the University of Florida, needed some gut-it-out heroics on his final hole to maintain any hope of advancing to match play here at the 126th U.S. Amateur. Parker was among the wave of players who went off hole 11 at Merion, meaning his round concluded on the drivable par-4 10th.

“He had to birdie it,” Sherry began, eager to dish the blow-by-blow details only a mother can provide. “He went for it, hit the green, bounced back into the sand, and it was right on the edge, on the down slope of the trap. Like, he barely had a backswing. He had one leg out, kneeling, and he kind of, like, goes like this.” Here, Sherry contorted into an uncomfortable-looking position. “Inch from the hole,” she continued. “Wow, wow. Best shot I’ve ever seen. His caddie — he was like, ‘Best shot I’ve ever seen.”

Golf.title: This part of the bag is key for the U.S. Amateur at Merion
Golf.summary: As the best amateurs in the world begin match play at Merion Golf Club, see what part of their bag could be key at the U.S. Amateur. The post This part of the bag is key for the U.S. Amateur at Merion appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Merion Golf Club’s East course is certainly a lot more than just a the scorecard. At just 6,939 yards this week, Merion is one of the shortest courses in modern championship golf, but if you look a little closer at how the course arrives at that length, it paints a different picture.

Despite the yardage, there’s no shortage of long holes, as there are three par-4s over 480 yards (5,6 and 18), two par-3s over 230 yards — with a third that was stretched to 266 during the 2013 U.S. Open — and both par-5s measuring nearly 600 yards. On the flip side, five par-4s measure 365 yards or less, as well as a par-3 that’s just 119 yards.

Golf.title: At Merion, host of the 2026 U.S. Amateur, there's always magic in the air
Golf.summary: So many legends have won at Merion, like Hogan, Jones and Trevino. This championship, this course, follows golfers around forever. The post At Merion, host of the 2026 U.S. Amateur, there’s always magic in the air appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Mark Fulcher, the winning caddie at the 2013 U.S. Open at Merion with Justin Rose, is enduring a serious case of caddie envy this week, with the U.S. Amateur unfolding at Merion. Like all proper golf bums, Fooch (as the veteran British caddie is known throughout golf and at your better racetracks) knows that match-play golf is the game at its primal and purest best. This is, after all, a man who has caddied in seven Ryder Cups, seven Solheim Cups and one Presidents Cup, all contested at match play. The U.S. Am, like its British counterpart, is a match play event (after the two-day stroke play qualifier). At the 1930 U.S. Am at Merion, Bobby Jones completed golf’s version of the Grand Slam (it’s a bridge term) with an 8-and-7 victory in the 36-hole final over a gent named Eugene V. Homans. If you’re new to this whole thing, in match play every hole is its own one-hole contest. Jones had an eight-hole lead with seven holes to go. No more golf. Jones and his caddie, a local teenager named Howard Rexford, joyfully made the hike from the 11th green back to the club’s iconic white farmhouse clubhouse. There were no carts.

“Could you hit driver or 3-wood on one?” Fooch asked the other day, repeating a question posed to him and doing some oh-so-English stalling. The first hole at Merion is — well, what’s north of iconic? The first at Merion is a delicate tea-party par-4 with a ladies-at-lunch porch located a short lefty’s shank shot away. From there the hole is a wee uphill dogleg that, in U.S. Open stroke-play golf, is iron off the tee, wedge into the green, all day long, four straight days. But match play is a different animal.

Golf.title: LIV Golf team championship in Plymouth is canceled: report
Golf.summary: LIV Golf team championship in Plymouth is canceled: report Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
The worst-kept secret in professional golf is apparently out there now: There will be no LIV Golf event in Michigan this year. LIV has told players that the team championship event, scheduled to take place in Plymouth in three weeks, has been canceled, according to a report in The Telegraph on Wednesday, Aug. 12.

This would be the second LIV tournament to be canceled in 2026, after an event in New Orleans was called off in June. A cancellation of the event should come as no surprise. On Aug. 5, LIV announced a new lead investor but did not commit to the 2026 season finishing with the team championship at The Cardinal at Saint John's in Plymouth, scheduled for Aug. 27-30. And as Free Press columnist Carlos Monarrez pointed out, there was no visible signage or indication a tournament was coming to the course in the near future.

Golf.title: LIV Golf players told season finale is canceled, according to report
Golf.summary: LIV Golf players told season finale is canceled, according to report golfdigest.com
Golf.body:
After weeks of rumors, LIV Golf has informed its players that the season-ending event has been canceled, according to a report from the Telegraph. LIV Golf Michigan’s demise has been speculated for some time. Martin Kaymer said last month that the event had a “five percent” chance of happening, no infrastructure has been built on the host venue despite a scheduled date of Aug. 27, and a LIV announcer stated the Indianapolis event would be the final stop on the schedule. But LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil would not comment on the matter last week in New Jersey, only saying “We have not made any final formal decisions and hope to in the coming weeks.”

However, according to the Telegraph’s James Corrigan, players have now been told LIV Michigan won’t be held. As of writing, no official announcement has been made, and tickets are still available and being sold on LIV’s website.

Golf.title: LIV Golf season finale canceled, according to report
Golf.summary: LIV Golf will not host a team championship later this month, calling an end to the season earlier than expected. The post LIV Golf season finale canceled, according to report appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What has long been rumored has now been reported as reality: LIV Golf’s team championship in Michigan has been canceled. The season finale, which was scheduled for the end of August in Michigan, was already believed to be on the chopping block as early as July. Various reports suggested no on-site buildout at The Cardinal at Saint John’s, even as recently as this weekend. And now LIV is moving on, according to a report from The Telegraph, which said the league finally told its players it would not be held.

In recent weeks, most LIV players had little to say about the event, although Martin Kaymer told Today’s Golfer in late July that the team championship had about a 5% chance of happening. Now that reality finally arrived. Staffers were told to book travel home from next week’s event in Indianapolis rather than to Michigan, just a few hours up the road. And despite the dark clouds over its team championship, LIV itself has refused to announce it publicly. (When contacted by GOLF, the league declined to comment.) The event is scheduled to begin in two weeks.

Golf.summary: Defending champion Justin Rose addressed news that the FedEx St. Jude playoff event will not be part of the PGA Tour's top tier in 2028. The post Major champ mulls loss of playoff event amid PGA Tour schedule ‘shakeup’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Last year, Justin Rose capped a comeback season with a big playoff win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship. This week, the 2013 U.S. Open champion has a chance to defend his St. Jude title from last year. But it may be the final time.

While the FedEx St. Jude has been a FedEx Cup playoff event since 2022, that is about to change in a big way. Last week, the PGA Tour confirmed to GOLF that the tournament would not be included in the top tier of the overhauled Tour schedule in 2028. That means it will certainly not be a playoff event. Even worse, it might cease being a tournament altogether.

Golf.title: Explained: Why LIV Golf may face another OWGR headache even if the league does survive
Golf.summary: Explained: Why LIV Golf may face another OWGR headache even if the league does survive Golfmagic
Golf.body:
One of the most tedious debates since the emergence of LIV Golf was whether or not the breakaway tour deserved to be recognised by the sport's global rankings body. Fronted by Greg Norman, the renegade tour applied for Official World Golf Ranking (OWGR) accreditation shortly after its launch in July 2022.

The application was made before the landmark 150th Open at St Andrews, but it took the governing body until the following October to reject LIV's bid. The OWGR cited several reasons for its decision and urged LIV to make adjustments to its format, field sizes and pathways into the league.

Golf.title: Best logo in golf? Even the U.S. Amateur field can't resist Merion's distinctive mark
Golf.summary: The Merion logo, or components of it, are everywhere at the U.S. Amateur this week. And for good reason: Golfers can't get enough of it. The post Best logo in golf? Even the U.S. Amateur field can’t resist Merion’s distinctive mark appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Jack Davis owns about 70 golf shirts bearing Merion Golf Club’s familiar wicker-basket-and-scotch-broom logo and maybe another 30 pieces of outerwear emblazoned with the emblem. His Merion hat tally? Anyone’s guess.

“Even for us, we’re not desensitized to it,” Davis said Tuesday afternoon here in the pro shop at Merion, which this week is the host site of the 126th U.S. Amateur. Us is the staff that runs Merion’s charming, chock-full-o-merch golf shop (Davis is the director of golf), and it is the intoxicating lure of one of the game’s most iconic logos. They’re a funny old thing, golf-club logos — most are uninspired and forgettable, some are serviceable and then there are the precious few that break through the clutter: distinctive marks that are immediately recognizable, to golfers and sometimes even non-golfers. Sleepy Hollow (headless horseman). Maidstone (spouting whale). Augusta National (no description needed). Beauties all of ’em.

Golf.title: One of the U.S. Amateur's hottest golfers has its wackiest swing
Golf.summary: Jay Leng's unique, unorthodox swing is a homemade piece of art that won him the Western Amateur and has him dreaming big this week at Merion. The post One of the U.S. Amateur’s hottest golfers has its wackiest swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Ask Jay Leng Jr. to describe his swing, and he flashes a big smile. “I’d say it’s art,” the rising junior at Stanford told GOLF after the second round of the 2026 U.S. Amateur at Merion East outside of Philadelphia.

In a previous golf era, Leng’s unique swing wouldn’t have drawn a reaction. But in the age of super-optimized, ball-speed-chasing swings, Leng’s patented motion sticks out. He and his Stanford coach, Conrad Ray, would call it “abbreviated.” Leng takes the club back inside, but before it gets to shoulder level, he turns with the club face slightly closed to start his downswing. During his follow-through, his shaft gets almost parallel to the ground and then whips the club around, finishing it however feels best for that swing. No two are the same, and he has been known to leave the ground when going after one.

Golf.title: The hidden art of preparing for a U.S. Amateur at Merion
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joey Wuertemberger has four players in the field at the U.S. Amateur. Here's how they prepared. The post The hidden art of preparing for a U.S. Amateur at Merion appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Walking into a U.S. Amateur with four players gives you a unique perspective on preparation. They’re playing the same golf course, facing the same conditions and competing for the same championship, but that doesn’t mean they should prepare — or play the golf course — the same way. That has been one of my biggest focuses this week at Merion and Philadelphia Country Club.

My four players have very different games. One has tremendous power. Another wins with patience, positioning and putting. One relies heavily on precision and his scoring clubs, while another is a complete player who simply loves to compete. My job isn’t to give all four of them the same game plan. It’s to help each player understand where his strengths can give him an advantage, where his weaknesses can’t get exposed and how his particular game fits Merion.

Golf.title: The most terrifying shot of the U.S. Amateur at Merion might have already happened
Golf.summary: The U.S. Amateur is filled with white-knuckle moments for golf's top ams. But the most terrifying shot at Merion might have already been hit. The post The most terrifying shot of the U.S. Amateur at Merion might have already happened appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Drue Nicholas has achieved a lot in the world of competitive amateur golf. The 23-year-old from Egg Harbor Township, New Jersey, etched his name right next to Jay Sigel, the greatest amateur golfer since Bobby Jones, in 2025 when he became the first player since Sigel to win the BMW Philadelphia Amateur and the Philadelphia Open in the same year. Nicholas backed that up by winning the 2026 Philadelphia Open in a playoff before punching his ticket to the 2026 U.S. Amateur at Merion via a two-under round at the Llanerch Country Club qualifier.

The U.S. Amateur is a marathon golf week filled with white-knuckle moments for the world’s best amateur players, be they 17-year-old Miles Russell or 34-year-old accounting professor Brett Patterson. But the most terrifying shot of the week might belong to Nicholas.

Golf.title: LIV Golf just got new life but uncertainty remains
Golf.summary: LIV Golf just got new life but uncertainty remains The Week
Golf.body:
With Saudi Arabia ending its funding of LIV Golf after this season, the league is at a crossroads, moving away from its largest controversy while still in need of new financial backing. Now it appears LIV may have found some, announcing last week that it has secured investors to bring it into the 2027 season and beyond. But some major questions about the tour’s future linger.

LIV Golf has an “agreement in place with a lead investor, signed by the investor and approved by the board, to anchor the transaction and play a key role in supporting the path forward for the league’s next era, driven by and for the players,” the tour’s CEO, Scott O’Neil, said in a statement. O’Neil “didn’t identify the investor or how much money will be injected into the league,” said ESPN, though he hopes to “finalize terms in the coming weeks.”

Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. I bought an Odyssey Ai-ONE putter last year; this year’s model added a white half-circle on top for alignment. Rather than plunk down my credit card again, I bought white circle stickers, cut one in half, affixed it to my “old” putter and — voilà! — I have the new putter, or a reasonable approximation. But is it a Rules violation? — Thomas Kapp, Hartsdale, NY

Thomas, we have a name for your putter: the Kapp Sticky Half-Moon DIY. All we ask for is a 10 percent cut of future sales…. For definitive word, the USGA would certainly want to view at least an image of your modification; essentially, however, it depends upon the nature of the adhesive used to affix the sticker to the top of the clubhead.

Golf.title: The U.S Amateur's most important lesson comes from ... an accounting professor?
Golf.summary: When Brett Patterson qualified for the U.S. Open at 19, he thought golf was his future. Now he's back in the fray with a different lesson in hand. The post The U.S Amateur’s most important lesson comes from … an accounting professor? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — The U.S. Amateur Championship is a proving ground filled with lessons for golf’s youngest stars. But at this year’s edition at Merion East, one important lesson will come not from the Hugh Wilson design on the outskirts of Philadelphia, but from a 34-year-old accounting professor competing for the title.

One whose journey to the U.S. Am is different than most. Fifteen years ago, Brett Patterson was an ascending collegiate talent as a freshman at Middle Tennessee State University. At 19 years old, Patterson fired a second-round 62 at Hawks Ridge Golf Club in final U.S. Open qualifying to punch his ticket to the 2011 U.S. Open. Rory McIlroy romped to his first major title that week while Patterson shot 77-78 to miss the cut at Congressional.

Golf.title: What is Bryson DeChambeau talking about now?
Golf.summary: What is Bryson DeChambeau talking about now? Golfshake.com
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has always divided opinion. A bit like Patrick Reed, he is a Marmite golfer - you either love him or you hate him. You never quite know what you are going to get with him, whether it is his thrilling attacking play and monstrous drives or the rounds where he spends 18 holes up to his neck in thick rough. And he is never far away from controversy, such as the two-stroke penalty he suffered at The Open Championship for improving his lie.

In an exclusive with the New York Post, DeChambeau says he wants to see LIV Golf teams own "stadium" home courses and also wants to have the ability to play on the PGA Tour in addition to LIV.

Golf.title: Inside LIV Golf's wild week: Bryson, Trump and the mystery investor surfaces
Golf.summary: A frenetic week for LIV Golf at Trump Bedminster ended with appearances by President Trump and a representative from LIV's reported investor. The post Inside LIV Golf’s wild week: Bryson, Trump and the mystery investor surfaces appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BEDMINSTER, N.J. — As LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil walked the final few holes with the last group on a sweltering Sunday at Trump Bedminster, he had an inside-the-ropes special guest at his side: Ted Goldthorpe, the head of BC Partners Credit, which manages more than $10 billion globally across more than 300 investments. One of the latest companies Goldthorpe’s team reportedly has been kicking the tires on: yep, LIV Golf, which on Wednesday announced it had come to terms with an unnamed investor that will “carry and fund” the beleaguered league into 2027 and beyond.

LIV has not officially acknowledged BC Partners as its would-be funder, or lender. That news came to light via Bloomberg and the Financial Times, the latter of which reported that the deal will be consummated only if BC Partners and other possible investors receive assurances that enough of LIV’s A-listers will hang around beyond this season. Adding intrigue to the dealmaking is the fact that BC Partners is a lender to GSE Worldwide, the sports and entertainment marketing agency that represents LIV’s biggest star, Bryson DeChambeau, along with Joaquin Niemann, the 27-year-old Chilean who won his ninth LIV title here Sunday, with a three-shot win over Harold Varner. GSE said in a statement earlier this week that it had no involvement with BC Partners’ “potential financing transaction involving LIV Golf,” nor, the agency said, was it aware of any discussions happening between the two parties.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's clubs: What's the deal with his mysterious Titleist proto 3-wood?

Golf.body:
Michael Brennan is once again a winner on the PGA Tour, earning his second PGA Tour victory and punching his ticket to the FedEx Cup playoffs at the Wyndham Championship. Brennan collected his second victory in the last three weeks for Titleist’s mysterious GTS prototype 3-wood. The 24-year-old was actually the first player to be spotted with the unknown GTS fairway wood option at the Texas Children’s Houston Open during the GTS driver launch, but didn’t game the prototype until two months later at the Charles Schwab Challenge.

Titleist has thus far not commented on the prototype, but we can speculate that the GTS may have similar characteristics to the GT1 3Tour fairway wood that both Brennan and Cameron Young — who switched to the prototype this week — previously played.

Golf.title: Michael Block walks off course at senior event, is DQ'd
Golf.summary: Michael Block received one of the strangest DQs of the 2026 golf season on Sunday, and neither side seems entirely sure why. The post Michael Block walks off course at senior event, is DQ’d appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It’s the senior tour DQ heard ’round the world, if such a thing exists. Michael Block’s disqualification from the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship in Aberdeen, Scotland was not just shocking because it was, well, a story of a DQ from a Legends Tour event. It was shocking because it arrived with a torrent of criticism, a two-shot penalty for showing up late to the tee box, a series of competing accusations … and a much, much larger dose of confusion.

So, what exactly happened? Let’s recount the facts. Things were not going well for Michael Block, senior golf sensation, at the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship. He’d posted three consecutive over-par scores at Trump International — 76-73-78 — leading into Sunday’s final round, an 11-over score that would have been good for 49th place in the competition.

Golf.title: Why men should pay attention to Asterisk Talley's winning U.S. Women's Am clubs
Golf.summary: Asterisk Talley won the 2026 U.S. Women's Amateur. How she builds the bag can teach the weekend warrior a few lessons. The post Why men should pay attention to Asterisk Talley’s winning U.S. Women’s Am clubs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Seventeen-year-old Asterisk Talley took home the trophy at this year’s U.S. Women’s Amateur at The Honors course. After multiple delays due to storms, the final match came down to Talley and No.1 seed 17-year-old Anna Iwanaga. Talley ended up victorious, winning 8&6 over Iwanaga in the 36-hole final match with nine birdies and an eagle. If you listen to our Fully Equipped Podcast, you’ll often hear us say that the women’s game has more relatable equipment to the average golfer, so let’s see what we can learn from Talley’s winning TaylorMade setup.

The good news for the guys? This is probably one of the more “crafty” women’s setups I’ve seen. It’s a fun bag. Yup. Jumbo. On all her clubs. I had a chance to hang out with Asterisk for a little bit on the range at Whirlwind Golf Club earlier this year, and it was the first thing I noticed too. I asked her about it, and she had a pretty simple answer for me.

Golf.title: Asterisk Talley's U.S. Women's Amateur win delivered the message she'd been sending
Golf.summary: Asterisk Talley's dominant U.S. Women's Amateur win was years in the making. Afterward, the message she'd been sending was finally received. The post Asterisk Talley’s U.S. Women’s Amateur win delivered the message she’d been sending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Four months ago, Asterisk Talley stood on the 12th tee at Augusta National with seven holes between her and the Augusta National Women’s Amateur title. The 17-year-old had just made her first bogey of the week at the 11th but was still in command of the tournament.

Twenty minutes later, Asterisk Talley had lost the tournament after a quadruple bogey that saw her put two balls in the water from the back bunker. After limping home with tears in her eyes, Asterisk Talley stood at the mic and showed grace as she answered questions about a brutal life lesson delivered in public. A month later at the Chevron Championship, Asterisk Talley explained that while those scars were painful, she realized they were the price of wanting to be great. That you can’t win unless you’re willing to risk being broken.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's Wyndham win ended with touching reminder from his mom
Golf.summary: Michael Brennan won the Wyndham to make the playoffs. After his win, his mom reminded him of something else that came with his win. The post Michael Brennan’s Wyndham win ended with touching reminder from his mom appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Michael Brennan didn’t want to be done playing golf. The 24-year-old had been in contention the past two Sundays and entered the Wyndham Championship feeling like his game was finally where it needed to be. There was only one problem. After struggling for most of the year, Brennan entered the PGA Tour’s regular-season finale ranked 105th in the FedEx Cup Playoff standings. He needed a three-way tie for second or better at Sedgefield Country Club to keep his season going to Memphis.

Brennan opened with rounds of 66 and 65 to enter the weekend three shots off the pace set by Beau Hossler. A sizzling Saturday 63 pulled Brennan even with Hossler and then he put his foot on the gas on Sunday, reeling off five straight birdies on the front nine to take the lead and put the pressure on Hossler, who needed a win to keep his season alive, to catch him down the stretch.

Torque GC Captain Joaquin Niemann extended his record to nine tournament wins with a clutch back-nine performance to shoot a 2-under 69 and win by three shots. “A great feeling to have, especially coming down the stretch on how tough this golf course is,” said the 27-year-old Chilean, the league’s youngest captain.

Golf.title: Back in stock! Shop Mizuno's Pro M-13 irons
Golf.summary: Mizuno's new Pro Modern Series irons were an immediate hit when first released, and now the popular Pro M-13s are back in stock. The post Back in stock! Shop Mizuno’s Pro M-13 irons appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Mizuno’s new Pro Modern Series irons were an immediate hit when they were first released in January, and now the popular Pro M-13s are back in stock at Fairway Jockey. Featuring easy-launch technology in the long irons, more stability in the mid-irons and forged-steel construction in the short irons, the Mizuno Pro M-13s have a Tour-style look, and are designed for players looking for speed, forgiveness and playability without sacrificing Mizuno’s traditional shaping and feel.

Could the Pro M-13s be a fit for your game? “M-13 is for the player who doesn’t quite have the precision or consistency to wield a single-piece forging like the Pro S-3, or perhaps a great ball striker who would like to regain some lost speed,” wrote GOLF associate gear editor Jack Hirsh at the time of the clubs’ release. “The irons will have a wide range of handicap users and could make it into the bags of elite players as a long iron replacement.

Golf.title: Brooks Koepka offers unflinching assessment of PGA Tour season: 'Pathetic'
Golf.summary: After missing out on his final chance to make next week's FedEx Cup playoffs, Brooks Koepka offered a searing assessment of his season. The post Brooks Koepka offers unflinching assessment of PGA Tour season: ‘Pathetic’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Heading into the final regular-season event of the PGA Tour season, Brooks Koepka needed to conjure some magic. The five-time major winner left LIV and rejoined the PGA Tour in January, and the expectation was that the 36-year-old would pick up right where he left off, given the eight wins he had accumulated between 2015 and 2021. (Koepka won his 9th PGA Tour event and fifth major, the 2023 PGA Championship, while playing as a member of LIV Golf.)

But Koepka’s Tour re-entry didn’t produce the level of performance he was hoping for — at least relatively speaking. He made 10 of 15 cuts with six top-25 finishes, but never really contended for a title.

Golf.title: How Andrew Catalon became a part of the CBS Masters broadcast team
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, Andrew Catalon explained what it was like to be invited to join CBS' Masters broadcast team. The post How Andrew Catalon became a part of the CBS Masters broadcast team appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Before longtime CBS broadcaster Andrew Catalon starting calling golf tournaments, he realized the core CBS golf broadcast team was something special. On this week’s episode of Subpar, Catalon, who also works NFL and college basketball games for CBS, explained how he started calling golf tournaments — and what it was like to invited to join CBS’ Masters broadcast team.

“I did the digital, featured group and that type, for 10 years,” Catalon told hosts Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz. “My first one was [Charl] Schwartzel [in 2011]. And then 2020 with Covid, I did it from my basement and that was my last one, digital. 2021 was my first one on the main broadcast.

BEDMINSTER: Joaquin Niemann’s dominant week hit its first speed bump, but he remains well positioned to secure his second LIV Golf title of the season. To set the scene, the events happened during a member-member championship at WingHaven last weekend. The golfer in question, who we won’t name to avoid piling on, is a plus-2 handicap and played college golf at a junior college before having what he described to ESPN as “a cup of coffee” at Eastern Illinois University.

Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau is “100 percent” confident in LIV Golf’s future after CEO Scott O’Neil announced earlier this week that the league had found a “lead investor” to keep it alive past 2026. Golf.title: Want to hit a proper pitch? Master this 1 key
Golf.summary: Top 100 Teacher Krista Dunton explains why getting too steep can cause pitching problems — and how to avoid it. The post Want to hit a proper pitch? Master this 1 key appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One key to hitting a great pitch shot is balancing steep angles in the setup with shallow angles during the motion. If you get too steep in the swing, the leading edge can dig and create inconsistent contact. Here’s how to keep that from happening.

At address, keep your hands neutral with minimal shaft lean, while your head and chest are slightly ahead of the ball. With this setup, you’ll create the necessary steepness in the body to hit a proper pitch. Now, for the shallow motion. Set the clubface open at address and un-cock your wrists.

Golf.title: Can't find a hat without a logo? Blame a refrigerator salesman
Golf.summary: How do today's pros command seven figures for a hat sponsorship? It all started at the 1968 PGA Championship ... with a refrigerator salesman. The post Can’t find a hat without a logo? Blame a refrigerator salesman appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As with most things modern in golf, Arnold Palmer played a part in the evolution of golf headwear. His win at the 1954 U.S. Amateur wasn’t just the King’s first step to the throne; photographs from his quarterfinal win are among the earliest of an elite golfer wearing a ball cap.

Flip your lid a decade-plus later: Another King — Lou, senior vice president of marketing at Amana Refrigeration — is watching Julius Boros outduel Arnie to victory at the 1968 PGA Championship in Texas. History has it that at one point in the television broadcast, Boros pulled an Amana-branded promotional hat from his golf bag to protect against the blazing San Antonio sun.

Golf.title: Brad Faxon recalls his wild ride at the '85 Honda Classic — with Michael Bamberger on the bag
Golf.summary: In 1985, Brad Faxon hired Michael Bamberger to caddie for him at the Honda Classic — and the experience made a lasting impact. The post Brad Faxon recalls his wild ride at the ’85 Honda Classic — with Michael Bamberger on the bag appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In 1985, second-year pro Brad Faxon and aspiring writer Michael Bamberger were two kids trying to figure it out. Faxon was in search of his game, Bamberger in search of a gig. Here the golfer-coach-broadcaster recalls their wild ride at the ’85 Honda Classic, where one of them passed go and the other — well, Faxon tells the rest.

On a late-fall day in 1984, after my rookie season on the PGA Tour had wrapped up, a personal letter arrived at my new townhouse in Orlando. Personal letters had a lot of impact in those days, and this one landed with a particular thud. It was written on a manual type-writer and, though the tone was modest, it went on for pages. The author told me about his own play as a bogey golfer, his experience as an occasional caddie while in high school and his first postcollege job as a reporter at a weekly newspaper on Martha’s Vineyard, an island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts. Eventually, he made his pitch: Was I looking for a caddie for the 1985 golf season, and, if so, could he throw his hat in the ring?

Badminton.title: ‘Good Spirit and Just Hungry for a Medal’
Badminton.summary: ‘Good Spirit and Just Hungry for a Medal’ BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Far from letting his close second round loss at his home BWF World Championships dispirit him, Christo Popov used it as a springboard for a spectacular 12 months. Last year he was close to taking out top seed Shi Yu Qi in the Round of 16 in front of a delirious crowd in Paris; Shi would survive and go on to win the title.

For Popov, there was much to take from that performance. Since then, he has been among the most impressive players on the circuit. He would make history for France in winning the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals; this year would see him win the European Championships, spearhead France into the final of the BWF Thomas Cup, and win his first Super 750 tournament in Japan.

Badminton.title: India's BWF World Championships Wait Ends After 17 Years — Full Host History
Badminton.summary: India's BWF World Championships Wait Ends After 17 Years — Full Host History Sportstar
Badminton.body:
New Delhi will host the BWF World Championships from August 17, as the Badminton World Federation’s most prestigious tournament returns to India after 17 years. Hyderabad staged the event first, back in 2009, and New Delhi’s turn marks the 30th edition of a championship that dates back to 1977.

Copenhagen has hosted the Championships five times — more than any other city — with Jakarta and Birmingham next on three and two appearances respectively. New Delhi’s 2026 edition also brings the tournament back to Asia after four years, following Tokyo’s staging in 2022.

The 2026 BWF World Championships are set to bring the biggest names in badminton to New Delhi from August 17 to 23. The tournament will mark the 30th edition of the prestigious event and will return to India for the first time since 2009. However, despite being one of the most important tournaments on the badminton calendar, the World Championships do not offer prize money to the winners or runners-up.

Why is there no prize money at the BWF World Championships? According to Olympics.com, the BWF World Championships do not carry prize money. The tournament is classified by the Badminton World Federation as a Grade 1 Major Event, placing it alongside major competitions such as the Olympic Games, Thomas Cup and Uber Cup. The absence of prize money is linked to the nature of the competition, where players represent their countries and compete for the prestigious World Championship title, medals and national honour.
